summary.headline: Jindal Saw Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT fell to INR35 crores (from INR91 crores in Q1) as EBITDA dropped to INR312 crores on MENA disruption and water-segment softness.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 0.8% QoQ to INR4,523 crores and 6% YoY, but EBITDA fell to INR312 crores from INR420 crores in Q1, and PAT fell to INR35 crores including a INR27 crore tax credit. Management attributed the weakness to delayed Saudi job-work shipments, logistics cost inflation, coking coal costs in DI pipes, low utilisation in water pipes, Abu Dhabi DI plant underutilisation, and pellet margin pressure. Standalone net debt declined to INR2,245 crores from INR2,346 crores. Management guided H2 to be better than H1, with margins expected to move toward double digits from Q3/Q4 as oil and gas orders ramp.

segments.name: Standalone DI / water pipes
segments.commentary: Lower execution in domestic water business and coking coal cost spikes compressed margins; management says ductile facilities are fully booked for about one year, but EPC payment delays are slowing execution. Export DI orders expected to reduce domestic concentration.

segments.name: Seamless pipes
segments.commentary: API licence reinstated in June 2026, enabling bids on key orders; the business is rebuilding its order book, with margin benefit expected in coming quarters, though the immediate impact in Q2 was limited.

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: Margins hit by high stripping ratio, low-grade iron ore, and higher diesel prices; management says this may persist to some extent. ROM quantum is unchanged, and the EC application is under discussion with MoEF.

segments.name: Abu Dhabi DI subsidiary
segments.commentary: Q2 deliveries were 29,000 tonnes vs 34,000 tonnes in Q1; utilisation about 50%. Order book of about USD195 million for 177,000 tonnes gives 9-12 months of visibility; still EBITDA-positive but margins lower.

segments.name: Jindal Hunting JV (51%)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR9.70 crores with a loss of INR1.5 crores, due to suspension of API licence; licence now reinstated.

segments.name: US entities
segments.commentary: Described as consistent and contributing positively, mainly from job work in double jointing, coating and helical anchors. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY27 to be better than H1 and gross margins to move toward double digits from Q3/Q4 as oil and gas and export orders ramp; no exact numbers given.
Volumes in FY27 expected to exceed FY26 volumes, as H1 pipe volumes were above the prior-year H1.
Execution of new LOI-based orders expected from February-March 2027, with production towards the end of the year; utilisation improvement expected from Q4.
Abu Dhabi seamless pipe plant (300,000 tpa, about USD330 million, KEZAD) targets commercial operation in FY28-FY29; financial closure expected in coming months.
Saudi SAW JV (51% Jindal Saw, 49% Buhur) with two 300,000 tonne lines is in land and LC stage; no orders expected before commissioning in FY28-FY29.
Saudi DI finishing facility put on hold; Saudi market to be served from Abu Dhabi.
capex_capacity: Effective capacity about 2.3 million tonnes; effective utilisation about 67%. Management says 80% is not achievable soon, with the highest-ever volume about 1.8 million tonnes in FY25 and best execution level about 75%.
Abu Dhabi DI plant operating at around 50% utilisation; sales restricted to customers within trucking range.
Abu Dhabi seamless plant: 300,000 tpa, about USD330 million; long-lead equipment procurement underway with LCs and advances.
Saudi JV: land secured and LCs for long-lead items established; interim financial closure expected over the next few months.
Management is evaluating capex in India and MENA while reducing working capital (inventory and receivables fell in Q2).
demand_pricing: Standalone confirmed order book about USD1.135 billion (about INR10,700 crores); LOIs about USD625 million (USD430 million CIS, USD50 million South East Asia, and about USD145 million domestic/other), with a mix of export and domestic.

About USD575 million of LOIs were received pre-board-meeting, of which about USD425 million is oil and gas export. Management says the likelihood of LOIs not converting is very low; firm orders expected in a couple of weeks.

A roughly 6 lakh tonne Saudi job-work order has been delayed by the Middle East war; buyer is also the Saudi JV partner. Job-work value is conversion only (raw material supplied by the buyer), so it is only 28% of export value despite 41% of export volume.

Margin per kg fell from about INR51 to about INR41 over recent quarters; the mix shift is attributed to water-sector dominance, which is low margin. Export orders are seen as more profitable than domestic water orders; oil and gas margins are similar to exports.
Domestic water market faces oversupply; Jal Jeevan Mission funds are releasing slowly, and future orders will come through state governments.
Saudi Arabia imposed anti-dumping duty of 16%-30% on Indian DI pipe exporters; Jindal Saw is not affected as Abu Dhabi supplies Saudi, which may let it gain share.

qa_highlights.question: How firm are the new LOIs and when will they translate into dispatches? Can they replace delayed MENA volumes at comparable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on margins. Conversion risk is low; production starts around February-March, with new-order output towards year-end. The 6 lakh tonne Saudi job-work volume is not being replaced; the team is seeking alternative logistics with the buyer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the effect of Saudi anti-dumping duty on DI pipes and the Saudi SAW plant order intake?
qa_highlights.answer: Jindal Saw India does not export pipes to Saudi, so it is not liable; Indian peers face 16%-30% duties. The Saudi SAW plant has no orders yet, since commercial operation is targeted for FY28-FY29 and orders need inspection and approval first.

qa_highlights.question: Gross profit per kg has fallen from INR51 to INR41. When can it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a return to FY25 levels; margins are expected to trend upward from Q3 as oil and gas and export mix improves, with double digits possible from Q3/Q4.

qa_highlights.question: When will utilisation reach 80%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 80% depends on order execution; improvement expected from Q4, with the best-ever execution level about 75%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the LOIs fully FOB?
qa_highlights.answer: Export contracts are generally CIF; pricing includes a cushion for freight and other volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Why is export volume 41% but value 28%?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6 lakh tonne job-work order carries conversion value only, since the buyer supplies raw material. Management agreed to consider separate disclosure.

qa_highlights.question: Pellet margin pressure and EC status?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are hit by high stripping ratio and low-grade ore, with deeper mines. The EC application is pending with MoEF; ROM stays at the same level, so no EC enhancement is needed.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook from JJM and domestic water orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Ductile facilities are booked for about a year; the constraint is EPC payment delays across states. Future orders will come via state governments rather than JJM.

risks_watch: Conversion of about USD575 million of LOIs (of which about USD425 million oil and gas export) into firm orders; management expects firm orders within a couple of weeks, with production from February-March 2027.

Delayed ~6 lakh tonne Saudi job-work order (buyer is also the Saudi JV partner); management is seeking alternative logistics and is not replacing the volume, so MENA utilisation may stay weak for some time.

Gross profit per kg fell from about INR51 to INR41; management targets a return toward FY25 levels and double-digit margins from Q3/Q4, but gave no exact numbers and declined to comment on margins for new orders.
Abu Dhabi DI plant at about 50% utilisation, with sales limited to trucking range; Q2 deliveries fell to 29,000 tonnes from 34,000 tonnes in Q1.
Pellet margins under pressure from high stripping ratio, low-grade ore and diesel costs; EC application for pellets still under discussion with MoEF.

Domestic water demand: EPC payment delays across states and a domestic oversupply; future orders to come via state governments rather than JJM. Effective utilisation about 67% with 80% not expected soon.
key_quotes: The main challenge is not other order cancellation, but rather delay in shipping and revenue recognition.

So, we can expect Q3, Q4 onward that the margins will be moved towards, you know, double-digit and we are expecting and we expect that very soon this situation will be same what we were doing few quarters back.
We are we are, like, we are not replacing the capacity. For some time, the capacity might not be fully utilized.
Right now, we can comment on H2 blended because things are so volatile. We are working out certain modalities to export even the job -work order also.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on order conversion and on H2 being better than H1, but cautious on margins, declining to give exact figures and calling H2 blended guidance hard given volatility. It was evasive on the Saudi job-work replacement and on Saudi SAW order timing, and was open that Abu Dhabi and the water segment remain weak.
